proposed_from.topic:
The sharp finite-population price of fractional causal variance bounds. For each integer N>=2 take three multisets x_a=(x_a1,...,x_aN) in [0,1]^N, repeats permitted. Fixed contrast c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2). Put F_a=N^-1 sum_i delta_x_ai. V_rel(x)=inf over all probability couplings pi with marginals(F1,F2,F3) of E_pi[(sum_a c_a Y_a)^2]. V_int(x)=min over permutations sigma2,sigma3 of N^-1 sum_i(c1 x_1i+c2 x_2,sigma2(i)+c3 x_3,sigma3(i))^2. Define Delta_N=sup_x[V_int(x)-V_rel(x)]. Population marginal means are fixed, so the identical gap holds for contrast variances. For N>=3, under complete random assignment with fixed positive arm sizes n1+n2+n3=N, the sharp estimator-variance upper bound based on the known marginals differs between fractional and realizable completions by (V_int-V_rel)/(N-1). No claim that all full marginals are observed in one experiment. Determine the sharp asymptotic order of Delta_N, with any necessary arithmetic subsequences explicitly resolved: derive an explicit rate sequence r_N and universal constants 0<a<=b<infinity such that a r_N<=Delta_N<=b r_N for all sufficiently large N (or exact zero exceptional N classified). Prove the upper bound by a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in N and rational-input bit length, that takes empirical marginals and an optimal rational fractional coupling and outputs N-row permutations with cost at most V_rel+b r_N. Prove the matching lower bound over the SAME three-arm scalar [0,1] class by explicit families. The exponent/log factors and proof mechanics are answer-open; no unverified rate is assumed. Translate the guarantee into computable two-sided certificates for the marginal-information sharp randomization variance, and provide a consistent plug-in estimator of its endpoints under complete randomization, deriving sampling error from the empirical marginal distributions. A generic finite LP or an arbitrary vanishing rate is insufficient. Grounding: Gao-Ge-Qian (AISTATS2025), Brennan et al. (ICML2025), Haus (2015), and Puccetti-Wang (2015); the new object is same-empirical-marginal fractional-versus-N-row squared-cost loss, not quantile-discretization error, a generic integer program, or ordinary bottleneck mixability. Consumer: three-arm contrast comparisons within published multi-arm trials such as ACTG175 (Hammer et al.1996). PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The informal draft derives ordered support-slope intervals from fractional LP duality, builds nested dyadic partitions, freezes integer masses from successive basic feasible tables, and repairs each marginal hierarchically. Its quadratic slack accounting gives a candidate universal upper bound 3456/N. An exactly certified four-row obstruction, padded with isolated dummy rows, gives 1/(46080N) for every N at least four. Thus the supported answer is a sharp 1/N rate within the original answer-open coordinates. Thirty-six rational implementation checks passed, using numerical bases only as proposals followed by exact rational verification. Repeated atoms, dyadic boundary contacts, replication parity, and the two-row case were checked; arbitrarily tiny rational gaps are covered by the bit-length argument rather than a floating-point LP experiment. The variance certificates concern the sharp upper endpoint, with sampling uncertainty separately retained.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the slope-interval bound, residual-to-repair accounting, and polynomial rational vertex extraction; no remaining structural mathematical gap was identified, but standard LP, tree-matching, quantile/gluing and sampling steps remain compressed.
EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the three load-bearing inequalities on exact optimal supports with ties and boundary contacts; stop this route on a counterexample, or on a verified same-marginal sharp-rounding prior-art collision.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/round1040_presolve_strongest.md. PRACTICAL LIMITATION: The useful numerical certificate is the actual primal-dual width. The loose universal 3456/N bound may be uninformative at ordinary trial sizes, and the sampling uncertainty is larger than the deterministic rounding term asymptotically.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest mathematical paper proves existence and failure of empirical Monge solutions for the opposite quadratic orientation and leaves quantitative error open. The closest causal paper identifies and estimates the unrestricted fractional coupling value but does not require one \(N\)-row science table. The selected kernel proves matching \(N^{-1}\) upper and lower orders for the original bounded scalar contrast class, supplies an exact-rational bit-polynomial rounding algorithm, and translates the loss into an order-\(N^{-2}\) variance-endpoint certificate. Quantile discretization changes the marginals, tensor rounding remains fractional, Haus controls a bottleneck objective, and Brennan et al. provide no universal analytic realization width.

seed_details.seed: Sharp \(N^{-1}\) same-marginal three-arm realization frontier with a bit-polynomial rounding algorithm
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, Introduction, Example 1, two-point-support theorem and proof, and Discussion; the Discussion asks for rigorous quantification of Monge error.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace their brute-force Monge comparison by dual tightness for the signed scalar squared cost; the first new step is the ordered support-slope interval inequality, followed by multiscale integer repair.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for empirical Monge--Kantorovich additive error, same-marginal permutation rounding, and three-marginal quadratic integrality gaps found only tensor-to-fractional-polytope rounding, quantile discretization, or bottleneck objectives.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic multi-marginal tensor rounding because exact marginals can already be restored in polynomial time.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existing tensor rounding outputs another fractional coupling; it does not output \(N\) common rows, and generic bounded-cost repair loses the quadratic dual-slope summability.
seed_details.burned_reason: The selected same-marginal rounding angle exhausted its bounded in-scope maximality improvements but remained below the field floor.

seed_details.seed: Exact zero-gap characterization through integral decomposability of the optimal dual-tight hypergraph
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, Theorem 1.1 and proof, joint-mixability section, and Conclusions item (i) on the missing characterization.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace unrestricted rearrangement existence by an if-and-only-if decomposition of an optimal dual-tight three-partite support into \(N\) unit-margin hyperedges.
seed_details.destination_search: Haus (2015), Emami and Pass (2025), and Friesecke (2019) settle hardness or isolated Monge cases but not a cost-specific zero-gap certificate for arbitrary repeated scalar atoms.
seed_details.red_team: Impossible as a useful theorem because Haus proves three-column complete mixability strongly NP-complete.
seed_details.rebuttal: A verifiable dual-tight hypergraph certificate can be necessary and sufficient without being polynomial-time decidable in full generality, but the hardness sharply lowers feasibility relative to the rate theorem.

seed_details.seed: Sampling-without-replacement plug-in certificates for the realizable three-arm sharp variance endpoint
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, Introduction, Lemma 1 and proof, sharp-bound plug-in construction, Proposition 1, and Discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The bivariate quantile coupling is no longer automatically row-realizable; first insert a certified fractional-to-row band, then propagate finite-population empirical-marginal error through both endpoints.
seed_details.destination_search: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025), Brennan et al. (2025), and Li and Ding (2017) separately cover fractional plug-ins, integer completions, and design-based asymptotics, but not their same-\(N\) three-arm combination.
seed_details.red_team: A routine consequence of the Lipschitz continuity of bounded quadratic transport values.
seed_details.rebuttal: Continuity controls the fractional endpoint only; the contribution requires a realizable endpoint, a non-double-counted deterministic band, and hypergeometric marginal error under one fixed finite population.

seed_details.seed: Fixed-\(K\) and contrast-geometry dependence of the fractional-to-row quadratic loss
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, Introduction, MOT formulation, Theorem 1 and proof architecture, finite-support exchange lemma and proof, and Discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The three-table basic-support decomposition must become a \(K\)-marginal discrepancy or flow decomposition that repairs one coordinate without reopening all earlier coordinates.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing fixed-\(K\) MOT, permutation schedules, rank-one quadratic costs, and integrality gaps found arbitrary-\(K\) fractional algorithms and bottleneck hardness but no matching \(N,K,c\) additive frontier.
seed_details.red_team: A routine induction on the three-arm repair theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The residual support becomes a \(K\)-partite hypergraph and the nested repair invariant fails under naive induction; the dependence on contrast sparsity and norms is itself open.

seed_details.seed: One-schedule simultaneous rounding of a finite family of contrast covariance directions
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, covariance example in the setup, quadratic-form theorem, dual proof, and Discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A scalar optimal support cannot be fixed first; the proof must construct one schedule controlling a uniform support function over several quadratic directions.
seed_details.destination_search: Targeted searches found directionwise fractional transport and general integer programs, but no Hausdorff rate between fractional and one-schedule covariance images.
seed_details.red_team: Follows by applying the scalar theorem to a contrast net and taking a union bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: Separate scalar schedules need not coincide, and a net argument does not construct one potential-outcome table attaining all directions simultaneously.

seed_details.seed: Uniform-convexity frontier for same-marginal \(p\)-power contrast costs
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, finite-support support-sum lemma and proof, and Discussion question on relations among \(p\)-norm approximate mixability notions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The exact quadratic slack identity must be replaced by the modulus of uniform convexity or smoothness of \(|\cdot|^p\), with separate regimes at \(p<2\) and \(p>2\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for approximate joint mixability under \(p\)-norms found qualitative dependence notions and continuous-marginal discretization bounds, not same-empirical-marginal Monge loss.
seed_details.red_team: A direct substitution of the standard \(L^p\) smoothness inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: The dual slope partitions and repair charges change exponent at the nonsmooth origin, so neither the rate nor the matching obstruction follows by substitution.

seed_details.seed: Stratified and covariate-conditional realization bands with globally allocated row budgets
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, Introduction, sharp-bound theorem, asymptotic plug-in argument, and Discussion on block-randomized designs.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Conditional fractional plans must be rounded within strata whose denominators differ, then residual row budgets must be allocated across strata without violating global arm counts.
seed_details.destination_search: Recent conditional optimal-transport work estimates covariate-aware fractional bounds, but the searched conditional-MOT and finite-row pairing did not reveal a realizability theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying the three-arm theorem stratum by stratum.
seed_details.rebuttal: Small or growing numbers of strata create incompatible denominators and a global allocation problem; the naive sum can be nonvanishing when strata remain small.

seed_details.seed: Rounding-aware optimal arm allocation minimizing the certified worst-case randomization variance
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv source, Introduction, integer-program construction, asymptotic-validity theorem and proof, and Conclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote the fixed counts \(n_a\) to integer decision variables and derive KKT conditions for the fractional allocation before certifying the discrete allocation with the realization band.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pair Neyman allocation with marginal-information sharp multi-arm variance bounds, but no result found an optimal integer allocation that internalizes a finite-row transport certificate.
seed_details.red_team: The rounding term does not depend on allocation, so ordinary Neyman allocation solves the problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the universal-bound level that objection largely holds; only data-dependent certificate widths can affect integer allocation, leaving too little theorem-level separation for the first version.

proposed_from.literature_map: Selected frontier seed: Emami and Pass (2025, Introduction, Example 1, two-point theorem, Discussion) establish that uniform empirical quadratic MOT may lack a Monge optimizer and explicitly call for quantitative error bounds; Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2 and Section 3) gives the closest finite-polytope non-Monge geometry; Haus (2015, Theorem 3 and approximation section) separates exact mixability hardness and bottleneck approximation from additive mean-square loss; Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, Sections 2--3, Theorem 1, finite-support lemma) supply the causal fractional target and coordinate-exchange geometry; Altschuler and Boix-Adser\`a (2023, Algorithm 3) round approximate tensors only back into the fractional transport polytope; targeted searches found no same-empirical-marginal, same-\(N\), scalar signed-quadratic additive frontier. Zero-gap seed: Puccetti and Wang (2015, Theorem 1.1, joint-mixability section, Conclusions) provide rearrangement language and an explicit characterization gap; Haus proves generic hardness, while Emami--Pass and Friesecke provide isolated Monge/non-Monge cases, so an exact certificate is not subsumed but is less feasible. Endpoint seed: Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Lemma 1, equations (7)--(11), Proposition 1) provide the two-arm sharp plug-in exemplar; Gao--Ge--Qian supply fractional estimation, Brennan et al. (2025, Sections 2--5) supply integer completion and asymptotic-validity context, and Li--Ding (2017, Theorems 3--4) supply the fixed-population randomization framework; no closer source combines a three-arm realization band with sampling-without-replacement endpoint error.
